issues.legal_issue: Acquisition for an integrated public development project constitutes acquisition for a public purpose, and a reviewing court should not substitute its assessment for the government’s absent a basis for interference.
material_facts: The land was acquired for expansion and systematic development of a tourist complex, including a parking area near a fairground.
The project was presented as requiring integrated and planned development of the complex.
The acquisition was challenged on the ground that the stated purpose was not genuinely public.
issues.conclusion: The development of the tourist complex, including the adjacent parking area, was a public purpose, and the acquisition was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sooraram Pratap Reddy v. District Collector, Ranga Reddy District (2008) 9 SCC 552, an acquisition project must be considered as a whole and assessed for its larger public interest rather than by separating its components. Infrastructure development is a legitimate public purpose; the government is prima facie the best judge of that purpose, although its decision remains subject to judicial scrutiny, and a writ court should not normally substitute its judgment for the government’s.

predicates.acquisition_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.integrated_development_project: The acquiring authority proposed a coordinated project whose components were intended to be developed together.
predicates.identified_public_need: The acquiring authority identified a public need that the project was intended to serve.

issues.definition: When an acquisition is challenged, the project is integrated, and an identified public need supports it, the acquisition is for a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation do not prevent acquisition when an overriding public interest conflicts with a private benefit.
material_facts: The landowner had obtained permission for a change in land use and had pursued approvals for a hotel project.
Construction was prevented for a period by a court order, and the landowner relied on the permissions and project-related directions to claim promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation.
The State acquired the land for development of a public tourist complex and related parking facilities.
issues.conclusion: The claimed promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation did not justify quashing the acquisition because the public interest prevailed over the landowner’s private interest.
issues.legal_principle: A.P. Pollution Control Board II v. M.V. Nayudu (Retd.) (2001) 2 SCC 62 states that there can be no estoppel against a statute. Monnet Ispat and Energy Limited v. Union of India (2012) 11 SCC 1 holds that legitimate expectation need not be fulfilled where overriding public interest requires otherwise. Hira Tikkoo v. Union Territory, Chandigarh (2004) 6 SCC 765 holds that legitimate expectation cannot be invoked where granting relief would harm the larger public interest. The public-welfare principle requires individual interests to yield where necessary for the public good.

predicates.acquisition_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.private_expectation_based_on_official_as: A private party relied on permissions, assurances, or official conduct as the basis for expecting that its proposed use of the land would continue.
predicates.overriding_public_interest: The acquiring authority pursued a public interest that outweighed the private party’s claimed benefit.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition is challenged, a private expectation rests on official conduct, and an overriding public interest is present, the private expectation does not prevent the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: A prior acquisition attempt that was abandoned does not by itself bar a later acquisition of the same land for a public purpose.
material_facts: An earlier attempt to acquire the land had been dropped after a court order restrained construction in the area.
After that order was modified, the State made a fresh decision to acquire the land for development of the tourist complex.
The landowner argued that the earlier abandonment showed that the later acquisition was not bona fide.
issues.conclusion: The earlier acquisition proceedings having been dropped did not bar the later acquisition, which was made after the relevant court order had been modified and for a public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: State of Haryana v. Vinod Oil and General Mills (2014) 15 SCC 410 holds that there is no bar to a subsequent acquisition after land has been released from an earlier acquisition. In this case, the Court also relied on the changed circumstances following modification of the order that had restrained construction.

predicates.acquisition_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.earlier_acquisition_abandoned: An earlier attempt to acquire the same land was discontinued.
predicates.later_public_purpose_decision_after_chan: The acquiring authority made a later decision to acquire the land for a public purpose after circumstances relevant to the earlier discontinuance had changed.

issues.definition: When an acquisition is challenged after an earlier attempt was abandoned, a later public-purpose decision made after relevant circumstances changed is not barred by that abandonment.

issues.legal_issue: Permission to change the use of land does not, by itself, invalidate a subsequent acquisition of that land.
material_facts: The landowner had received permission to change the use of the land for a proposed hotel project.
The acquisition was made for a public development project.
The Court noted that construction had not commenced in accordance with the conditions attached to the change-of-use permission.
issues.conclusion: The change-of-use permission did not provide a basis for invalidating the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: State of Haryana v. Vinod Oil and General Mills (2014) 15 SCC 410 holds that permission for change of land use has no relevance to the validity of a land acquisition. Clause (f) of Rule 26-D of the Punjab Scheduled Roads and Controlled Areas Restriction of Unregulated Development Rules, 1965 required construction to start within six months and be completed within two years from the change-of-use order; the Court noted that construction had not been undertaken in accordance with that condition.

predicates.acquisition_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.land_use_permission: The landowner received official permission to use the land for a proposed development.
predicates.acquisition_for_public_purpose: The land was acquired for a project serving a public purpose.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition is challenged, the landowner had permission for a proposed use, and the acquisition serves a public purpose, that permission does not invalidate the acquisition.
